note: Hand-authored. `quote` is verbatim from https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9700 with line wrapping removed and nothing else changed. Not sealed: RFC 9700 is broad and only the row below is enumerated. A PKCE row was drafted here and REMOVED rather than kept — no test cites RFC 9700 §4.1.3, and PKCE enforcement belongs under RFC 7636 (a stub in this increment). Marking it covered to make the gate pass would be exactly the over-claiming the gate exists to catch. The code-replay row used to be a waiver filed under §4.5 with RFC 6749 §4.1.2's sentence as its quote; RFC 9700 states the recommendation in §4.2.4, quoted below, and #627 satisfies it.

requirements.quote: Therefore, [RFC6749] further recommends that, when an attempt is made to redeem a code twice, the authorization server SHOULD revoke all tokens issued previously based on that code.
requirements.applies: POST /oauth/token, authorization_code grant. A second redemption that is otherwise a valid request revokes the refresh-token family the first redemption started, and puts every access token issued from the code or in that family on the revocation denylist (see the oauth-2_1 rows for when that is not possible).
requirements.evidenceMatch: revokes the refresh family|family revoked|revokes the access token
